title: Siman 367
section: The Virtue of His Torah and His Holy Books

segments.he: שָׁמַעְתִּישֶׁאָמַר יֵשׁ לִי הַשָּׂגָה כָּזוֹ לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהָיִיתִי יָכוֹל לְהָבִיא עַל יָדָהּ אֶת מָשִׁיחַ, אֲבָל סִלַּקְתִּי הַכּל וְלָקַחְתִּי עַצְמִי אֶצְלְכֶם לְהַחֲזִיר אֶתְכֶם לְמוּטָב, כִּי זֶה גָּדוֹל מִן הַכּל, כִּי זַכָּאָה מָאן דְּאָחֵד בִּידָא דְחַיָּבָא. וְאָז הוֹכִיחַ אֶת אַנְשֵׁי-שְׁלוֹמֵנוּ מְאד וְאָמַר, כַּמָּה יְגִיעוֹת הָיוּ לִי
segments.en: (29.) They told me that when I drew close to him, he said in the presence of other people — not in my presence: "Blessed is G-d who has sent me a young man such that not even one word of my words will be lost anymore." And his intention was about me — that I should merit to write all his words that go forth from his holy mouth: whether Torah discourses, whether conversations — for they too are Torah. And even a single word should no longer be lost.
